challengeTypes: identify: In which state of matter do particles have a fixed shape and volume? (Solid vs Liquid vs Gas vs All of them)

sort: Drag each property to the correct state of matter (Fixed shape and volume = Solid | Takes shape of container, fixed volume = Liquid | Fills entire container = Gas | Particles very close = Solid | Particles can flow = Liquid | Particles far apart = Gas)
identify: What is the process called when a solid turns into a liquid? (Melting vs Freezing vs Evaporation vs Sublimation)

sort: Drag each state change process to its correct name (Solid to liquid = Melting | Liquid to solid = Freezing | Liquid to gas = Evaporation | Gas to liquid = Condensation | Solid to gas = Sublimation | Gas to solid = Deposition)
identify: At what temperature does water freeze? (0 degrees Celsius vs 100 degrees Celsius vs 50 degrees Celsius vs 25 degrees Celsius)

sort: Drag each example to the correct state change (Ice to water = Melting | Water to ice = Freezing | Water to steam = Evaporation | Steam to water drops = Condensation | Camphor disappearing = Sublimation | Naphthalene balls shrinking = Sublimation)
identify: What is sublimation? (Solid directly changing to gas without becoming liquid vs Liquid changing to gas slowly vs Gas changing to solid vs Solid changing to liquid)

sort: Drag each factor to how it affects evaporation (Increase temperature = faster evaporation | Increase surface area = faster evaporation | Increase humidity = slower evaporation | Wind blowing = faster evaporation | Cover the container = slower evaporation | More heat = faster evaporation)
extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) States of matter — Solid: fixed shape and volume, particles very close and only vibrate. Liquid: takes shape of container, fixed volume, particles close but can move. Gas: fills entire container, no fixed shape or volume, particles far apart and move freely. (2) Interconversion — states can be changed by heating or cooling. Heating adds energy, particles move faster. Cooling removes energy, particles slow down. (3) Melting and freezing — Melting: solid to liquid (ice to water at 0 degrees C). Freezing: liquid to solid (water to ice at 0 degrees C). Melting point = freezing point for the same substance. (4) Evaporation and condensation — Evaporation: liquid to gas (water to steam at 100 degrees C for boiling, but evaporation happens at all temperatures). Condensation: gas to liquid (steam to water droplets on a cold surface). Factors affecting evaporation: temperature (higher = faster), surface area (larger = faster), wind (more = faster), humidity (higher = slower). (5) Sublimation — solid directly changes to gas without becoming liquid. Examples: camphor, naphthalene balls, dry ice (solid CO2). Deposition is the reverse: gas directly to solid. Misconceptions: 'evaporation only happens at boiling point' (WRONG — evaporation happens at ALL temperatures, boiling is just rapid evaporation at a specific temperature), 'freezing and melting are the same' (WRONG — melting is solid to liquid, freezing is liquid to solid; they are opposite processes at the same temperature), 'sublimation is the same as evaporation' (WRONG — sublimation is solid directly to gas, evaporation is liquid to gas), 'particles in a solid do not move at all' (WRONG — particles in a solid vibrate in place, they do not flow but they do move slightly), 'gas has a fixed volume' (WRONG — gas has no fixed shape or volume; it fills whatever container it is in).
